text: optional entity identifiers (LEI and other scheme-typed identifiers)

comments.text: Scope IN promises support for 'other scheme-typed identifiers', but the Data model explicitly narrows the register to the LEI alone ('this register narrows it to the one identifier FCY uses — the LEI — held flat') and defers any second scheme to a hypothetical future widening. One of these should give: either drop 'and other scheme-typed identifiers' from Scope, or the data model needs a second identifier field/list now. As written, an implementer reading Scope alone would build more than the data model supports.

text: R2: WHILE a legal entity is retired, the system SHALL exclude it from selection for new business.

comments.text: R2 is a rule about consumers of the register, not the register — the Data model notes say so itself ('R2 ... binds consumers of the register, not the register itself') — and the only consumer that selects counterparties for new business (trade booking) is declared OUT of scope. There is no surface in this spec that can satisfy or test A2: the register's own screens never 'offer' a counterparty for new business. Either restate R2 as something this register actually guarantees (e.g. retired status is stored and exposed so consumers can filter — which the standard screens already do), or move the exclusion rule to the spec that governs the consuming screen. As written, A2 can never be demonstrated within this document's scope.

text: A lifecycle for records (draft / active / retired) so a defunct counterparty can be retired without losing its history.

comments.text: The lifecycle is declared in scope and the status field defaults to draft, but no requirement states the permitted transitions: can a draft go straight to retired, is retired terminal or can a record be reactivated, and does retirement differ from deletion for a draft that was never active? Without at least one rule on transitions, 'active' and 'retired' are free-text labels and R2's trigger state is whatever a user typed last. One requirement covering the allowed transitions (or an explicit statement that any status change is permitted) would close this.

text: R1: WHEN a legal entity is saved with an LEI that another record already carries, the system SHALL reject the save and name the conflicting record.

comments.text: The rejection itself is already the bean table's 'unique when present' rule on LegalEntity.lei, which the platform enforces and tests — so R1 and A1 largely restate it, and the two statements can drift apart if the rule ever changes. The only content R1 adds beyond the bean rule is that the error 'name[s] the conflicting record'. Consider narrowing R1 (and A1 with it) to just that message detail, leaving the rejection to the bean rule it derives from.

Summary of this spec in one line: a firm-wide register of legal entities — one new bean, LegalEntity (name required; LEI optional, unique when present, 20 alphanumeric; lifecycle draft/active/retired defaulting to draft) — realising the CDM type cdm.base.staticdata.party.LegalEntity as vocabulary, driven by FCY standing rule R7 (every counterparty carries an LEI). The bean table carries the data rules; the spec adds only R1 (a duplicate-LEI rejection names the conflicting record) and R2 (retired entities are excluded from new business), verified by A1–A3. Out of scope: the CDM Party type, natural persons, the LegalAgreement stack, and GLEIF live verification. Artifacts: the entity descriptor (entity_descriptors/cdm.party.LegalEntity.json) and the default form (ui/cdm.party.LegalEntity.js), both saved; four review comments above are still open.
